memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, his household and the whole community of Israel." - Lev 16:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Nobody else. Not another priest, not a helper, not a witness. Aaron goes in alone.

Picture the nation outside, waiting in silence. They cannot see. They cannot help. They cannot know what is happening behind that curtain. Everything depends on one man in a room they will never enter.

Now go to Gethsemane. Jesus takes three disciples with Him and asks them to stay awake — and they sleep. He is arrested, and they all flee. Peter follows at a distance and then denies Him. At the cross, He cries out: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? (Mark 15:34).

I have trodden the winepress alone; from the nations no one was with me (Isa 63:3).

He went in alone. Not because no one wanted to help, but because no one could. Only He could do this work.

And here is what it means for you: because He was alone then, you are never alone now. Never will I leave you; never will I forsake you (Heb 13:5). The abandonment He endured purchased a promise that you will not be abandoned.

Whatever room you feel alone in today, He has already been in a worse one for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you feel most alone right now?
2. What does it mean that Christ endured abandonment so you would not?
3. How does His promise never to leave you change today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You went into the darkness alone so that I would never be alone. Thank You for that promise. Be near to me today in the place where I feel most isolated. Amen.
